title: Coherent space slices and base-change functors
statement: Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, coherent diagrams, coherent comma categories and limiting cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and use the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of small spaces from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], formed in the next universe; write $\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. For a vertex $b$, define $\mathcal S_{/b}$ as the coherent comma simplicial set $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal S}\downarrow b)$, retaining the entire family of structure arrows. A coherent square is a map from the nerve of the subset poset $\mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ to $\mathcal S$. Its pullback condition means that its specified cone from the empty-subset vertex to the three nonempty-subset vertices is limiting; the cone cylinder sends $(p,t)$ to $\varnothing$ at $t=0$ and to $p$ at $t=1$. For an edge $f:A\to B$ in $\mathcal S$, a base-change functor along $f$ consists of a simplicial functor $G:\mathcal S_{/B}\to\mathcal S_{/A}$ and a coherent family of squares parametrized by $\mathcal S_{/B}$. The top horizontal edge is exactly the structure-arrow family after $G$, the bottom horizontal edge is exactly the structure-arrow family over $B$, the right vertical edge is the constant family $f$, and each object-square is a pullback in the preceding sense. These are data and a universal-property predicate, with no choice of $G$ from a mere existence theorem.

source.place: Construction 3.1.6.1 (coherent nerve of Kan complexes); Section 7.7.1 and Proposition 7.7.3.19 (05V1) for the canonical slice pullback functor; the subset-poset square and its specified cone are an explicit model of that pullback universal property.
